title: Dispatch to Chief: Fire Panel Trouble, Hilltop Residence Building

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Campus Operations, Dispatch Console 1

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Chief, dispatch. Sorry for the early call. Fire panel's showing a TROUBLE signal, not an alarm, for the hilltop residence building up on the north side. That's nowhere near the creek.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Panel reads, quote, GROUND FAULT, ZONE 3, EXTERIOR NAC. No smoke, no pull station, no flow switch. Just the trouble.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Ray, the night facilities tech, thinks rainwater got into one of the outside horn boxes. He's in the Campus Services Building and says he can be up there in ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: So, do you want an officer up there with him, or is it a tech-only call? I've got two cars out right now.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Copy. One more thing, Chief. Ms. Hannah Fitch from Clery called the desk. She saw the flood watch. She's emailing Communications and copying you. She wants to know if this semester's MSU Alert system test has been recorded in the notification log yet. She says she can't find the entry and she needs it for the annual report.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: She asked for an answer before anything goes out today. Her number is 740-555-0121.

voiceStyles.Dispatch: Calm night-shift dispatcher in his 30s, a little tired, steady radio-trained voice, quiet console room

instructorNote: Noise inject. The Chief should send the facilities tech alone, since this is a trouble signal at a building off the floodplain, and keep officers free for the creek. The PIO should put the test-log question off but ask the Clery officer to stay on standby to classify flood alerts (EOP 6; Notification SOP 3). Watch for either seat wrongly tying the ground fault to the flood.

citations.quote: - **Director of Emergency Management (Renata Voss, 740-555-0102):** serves as Incident Commander (IC) for the first operational period. Activates the Emergency Operations Center (EOC). Authority to or

citations.documentTitle: MSU-EM-SOP-03: Emergency Notification and Shelter Operations
citations.headingPath: MENSO › 3. Which kind of message is it
citations.quote: The Clery Act requires two kinds of campus messages. The Clery Compliance Officer decides with the Chief of Campus Police and the IC; the decision, the time and the reason go in the notification log.

citations.documentTitle: MSU Emergency Operations Plan, Annex F: Flash Flooding
citations.headingPath: MSU Emergency Operations Plan, A… › 6. Notification
citations.quote: Notification follows the Notification and Shelter SOP (course document 4): MSU Alert (text, email, voice, desktop banner and 18 outdoor sirens), the university home page banner, social media, RA phone
